title: CLAUDE.md and rules in fcp
bridge: A root CLAUDE.md is like a README for a new teammate. It is a short map of where things live and how to run checks. Except: it is loaded into every Claude session, so every line costs context. Detail belongs in path-scoped rules, skills and the brain instead.
intro: fcp has no root CLAUDE.md today, so every session starts without a map. This lesson writes one under 200 lines. It adds rules that load only when Claude edits a given area. And it points compliance questions at Vanil instead of copying policy text. Three small files, each with a reason.

picture.caption: The root file is a map; detail loads only when Claude touches a matching file or asks the brain.

steps.text: loads the root map at launch
reads cloud/rhinoCloud/x.py: the cloud rule loads now, not before
a how or why question goes to the brain, cited as path@sha
a policy or Vanta question goes to Vanil, never to a copied page

p: Run claude in an fcp checkout and type /context. Under Memory files you see what loaded: frontend/AGENTS.md (92 lines, through frontend/CLAUDE.md which only says @AGENTS.md), sdk/CLAUDE.md (167 lines), cloud/mcp-server/CLAUDE.md (248 lines). There is no root file, so a session that starts at the repo root knows nothing about the layout.

Claude Code's docs recommend under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md. Longer files cost more context and are followed less. The docs also say what belongs there: build commands, conventions, project layout. Anything that matters for only one part of the codebase moves to a path-scoped rule.

The root file has four sections: where things live, run and check, changes and PRs, knowledge. It links to what exists instead of copying it: README.md, frontend/AGENTS.md, sdk/CLAUDE.md, the be-repo-conventions skill.
The wording is calm: goals and reasons. The walls (protected paths, locked checks) live in hooks, rulesets and infrastructure, not in this file. A prompt is advice; a hook is a wall (lesson p8-4).
sections.because: We write the map in the words a new engineer would use, because the model reads it the same way. And a map is only useful when it is short.

code.text:
# fcp

Rhino Health's Federated Computing Platform in one repo: the cloud API, the on-prem client that runs inside
customer networks, the Python SDK and the dashboard.

## Where things live
- `cloud/rhinoCloud/`: cloud API (Django, DRF, Celery). Main app `rhinoCore/`.
- `client/rhinoOnPrem/`: on-prem client (Django, gRPC, RQ). It reaches the cloud over a reverse gRPC stream.
- `common/fcp_common/`: shared code, including the gRPC protos in `rhinoAgentRpc/` (`make protoc`; _pb2 files are committed).
- `sdk/`: the public `rhino_health` package. Read `sdk/CLAUDE.md` first.
- `frontend/`: the dashboard (Next.js, React). Read `frontend/AGENTS.md` first.
- `ohif/`: our fork of the OHIF DICOM viewer.
Area rules in `.claude/rules/` load by themselves when you open files in that area.

notes.text: The H1 is the repo name. The next lines say what the repo is in one sentence.
Where things live: one line per area, with the main app named.
The client reaches the cloud over a reverse gRPC stream. That one fact prevents many wrong assumptions.
common/fcp_common: the gRPC protos, make protoc, and the fact that _pb2 files are committed.
sdk/ already has its own CLAUDE.md. Point to it; do not repeat it.
frontend/ already has AGENTS.md. Same rule.
One line tells the reader that area rules exist and load by themselves.

sections.h: Run, check, PRs and the brain pointer
p: The second half names the commands. poe --help lists the dev tasks. Backend unit tests run through scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh. Frontend checks are npm run lint, check-types and test:unit (G7 adds npm run verify later, and G8-04 adds the verify-skill line).
The last section is the one brain pointer this ticket exists for. How and why questions go to the kb skill, which cites pages as path@sha.
sections.because: We send how and why questions to the brain instead of writing the answers here. The brain has owners and review dates, and this file does not.

code.text:
## Run and check
- `poe --help` lists the dev tasks (`poe cloud-up`, `poe cloud-migrate`, `poe backend-integration-tests`, `poe frontend-test`).
- Backend unit tests: `scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud` (or `client`).
- Frontend: `npm run lint`, `npm run check-types`, `npm run test:unit` in `frontend/`.
- Use fake seed data only (factories and TestDataCreator), never real customer data.

## Changes and PRs
- One change per PR. Title: `[FE] RH-1234: what changes for the user` (`[BE]` for backend).
- Cloud, client and sdk CI run on push; frontend CI runs on pull requests.
- Fill in `.github/pull_request_template.md`.

## Knowledge
How does X work, or why is it like this? Use the `kb` skill. It searches the R&D brain (RhinoHealth/rnd-kb) and
cites pages as path@sha. If a page is wrong, propose a fix.

notes.text: Run and check: poe tasks first, because they wrap the long docker commands.
Backend unit tests, cloud or client, through the existing script.
The three frontend commands that exist today.
Fake seed data only: factories and TestDataCreator. Never real customer data.
PR title style: [FE] RH-1234: what changes for the user. add-jira-links.yml reads the key from it.
A fact people get wrong: cloud, client and sdk CI run on push; frontend CI on pull requests.
The brain pointer: use the kb skill, cite path@sha, propose a fix when a page is wrong.

callout.text: Check it in a fresh session: /context shows the file's cost. Ask three real questions: where is the gRPC contract, how do I run cloud tests, how do I seed data. See that each answer starts in the right place.

p: A rule is a markdown file under .claude/rules/. With a paths list in its frontmatter, it loads only when Claude reads, writes or edits a matching file. Without paths it loads at launch like CLAUDE.md. That is the mechanism that keeps the root map short.

We add four: cloud.md (cloud/**, common/fcp_common/**), client.md (client/**), sdk.md (sdk/**), frontend.md (frontend/**), each 20 to 60 lines. sdk/ and frontend/ already have their own files, so those two rules hold only cross-area points. That is API back-compat with the published SDK, and tests on test IDs, not class names.

Each rule names the risky spots of its area. Migrations and table locks, proto changes and old clients, and the client's clean and raw (PHI) databases. Also SDK back-compat, and layouts from 760 to 1440 px.
sections.because: We put the cloud rule in front of the agent exactly when it edits cloud code. That is the moment a proto or migration mistake is made.

code.text:
---
paths:
  - "cloud/**"
  - "common/fcp_common/**"
---
# Working in the cloud service

Goal: a change that keeps the API, the SDK and installed on-prem clients working, with a test that shows it.

- Django project `cloud/rhinoCloud/`, settings `rhinoCloud.rhinoDjango.settings`; most code is in `rhinoCore/`
  (models/, views/, serializers/, services/, celery_tasks/).
- Tests: `scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh cloud`. Use the factory_boy factories in
  `rhinoCore/tests/test_factories/` and `CommonRhinoTestCase`. Prefer fakes to mocks.
- Changed a model? Add the migration and run `./manage.py makemigrations --dry-run --check`. Some ALTERs lock big
  tables; say so in the PR.
- Protos in `common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc/` are a contract with clients already installed at customers. Add
  fields; don't rename or remove them. Run `make protoc` and commit the _pb2 files.
- A changed response shape reaches the published `rhino_health` SDK: check how `sdk/` uses the endpoint first.
- Lint: black and isort at 120, flake8 (pre-commit runs them).
- For deeper patterns, load the be-module-cloud skill.

notes.text: paths: the globs that make this rule load. cloud/** and the shared fcp_common code.
A goal line, not a rule list: keep the API, the SDK and installed clients working, with a test.
Where the code is and what the settings module is called.
How to run tests, which factories to use, and 'prefer fakes to mocks' (lesson p10-4).
Migrations: makemigrations --dry-run --check, and say in the PR when an ALTER can lock a big table.
The proto contract: add fields, never rename or remove; make protoc; commit _pb2 files.
A changed response shape reaches the published SDK, so check sdk/ first.
For depth, load the be-module-cloud skill (moved into the be-guild plugin in G8-02).

sections.ifInstead: If instead the rule loads for a frontend file too, the paths list is wrong or missing. A rule without paths loads for everything.

sections.h: Point at Vanil, do not copy it (G6-13)
p: Compliance answers already have an owner and a source of truth: Vanta, kept in sync by Nave's compliance agent, Vanil. If we copied policy text into rnd-kb it would go stale, and agents would trust the stale copy. So the brain holds one pointer page and the kb skill gets one line.

Ask two people. Nave knows what Vanil exposes today (the connector or MCP endpoint) and who may use it. Ronen decides whether engineers and agents may query it. The connector URL goes to Platform for the managed MCP allow-list (G8-16).
sections.because: We write a pointer page instead of a copy because a pointer cannot go stale in the way a copied policy does.

code.text:
---
title: Where compliance and security-policy answers live
owner: "@<Nave's GitHub login>" # confirm with Nave; Security is the backup owner
reviewed: 2026-11-04
review_every: 90d
confidence: low
sources:
  - "<link to Vanil's connector docs, from Nave>"
applies_to: []
---
# Where compliance and security-policy answers live

The brain doesn't copy policies, Vanta tests or audit evidence. Vanil, Nave's compliance agent, already tracks
them, with Vanta as the source of truth and Jira for the work.

- Ask Vanil (through its connector): a policy's current text, why a Vanta test is red, a vulnerability ticket's due date.
- Ask Security (Ronen): whether data may go somewhere, a new vendor, an exception.
- Engineering pages may link to a policy; they never paste it.

notes.text: Owner: Nave's GitHub login (to confirm); Security is the backup owner.
The source is Vanil's connector docs, which Nave provides.
The body says plainly what the brain does not hold: policies, Vanta tests, audit evidence.
Ask Vanil for: a policy's current text, why a Vanta test is red, a vulnerability ticket's due date.
Ask Security (Ronen) for: may this data go there, a new vendor, an exception.
Engineering pages may link to a policy; they never paste it.

callout.text: PHI never enters a prompt. The Rhino MCP server reaches customer data on prod, so the allow-list (G8-16) lists only mcp-dev3. Vanil's connector holds policy text, not patient data, which is why it may be on the list.

lab.title: A map and a path-scoped rule in a scratch repo

worked.see: An empty repo with two areas.

worked.do:
printf '# scratch

## Where things live
- `cloud/`: the API (Python).
- `frontend/`: the dashboard (TypeScript).
Area rules in `.claude/rules/` load by themselves when you open files in that area.
' > CLAUDE.md

printf -- '---
paths:
  - "cloud/**"
---
# Working in cloud
Goal: a change with a test. Prefer fakes to mocks.
' > .claude/rules/cloud.md && printf 'def add(a, b):
    return a + b
' > cloud/app/calc.py && printf 'export const x = 1
' > frontend/src/x.ts
worked.see: One path-scoped rule and one file in each area.
Under Memory files you see ./CLAUDE.md. The cloud rule is not listed yet, because no cloud file has been read.

worked.do: In the same session ask: "read cloud/app/calc.py and tell me what the area rule says"
worked.see: Claude reads the file, the cloud.md rule loads, and the answer quotes 'Prefer fakes to mocks'.

worked.do: Ask: "read frontend/src/x.ts; which area rules apply?"
worked.see: No cloud rule: frontend/** does not match paths cloud/**.

lab.faded: Add .claude/rules/frontend.md with paths frontend/** and one line about tests on test IDs, not class names. Start a fresh session and check with one question per area that each rule loads only for its own files. The check command is the one you used above.
lab.alone: Count the lines of fcp's real context files (frontend/AGENTS.md, sdk/CLAUDE.md, cloud/mcp-server/CLAUDE.md) with wc -l. Then draft fcp/CLAUDE.md on a branch from the two G6-06 blocks. Run wc -l on it (it must be under 200). Open claude at the fcp root and check that /context lists it.
lab.done: Your scratch repo loads cloud.md only for cloud files. Your fcp CLAUDE.md draft is under 200 lines and shows under Memory files.

quiz.q: Where does the rule 'add proto fields, never rename or remove them' belong?

options.text: In fcp/CLAUDE.md, because it is important.
options.why: It matters only when editing cloud or fcp_common code; the root map stays a map.

options.text: In .claude/rules/cloud.md with paths cloud/** and common/fcp_common/**.
options.why: A path-scoped rule loads exactly when Claude edits that area.

options.text: In a brain page only, since pages are the source of truth.
options.why: A page explains why; the rule is what the agent must see at edit time. G6-07's page and this rule say the same thing on purpose.

quiz.q: Why does the brain not hold a copy of the security policies?

options.text: Policies are confidential and cannot be read by engineers.
options.why: Ronen confirms who may query Vanil; the reason is staleness, not secrecy.

options.text: A copy would go stale and agents would trust it; Vanta via Vanil is the source of truth.
options.why: That is the why of G6-13: one pointer page and one line in the kb skill.

options.text: Policies are too long for a one-screen page.
options.why: Length is not the issue; ownership and freshness are.

quiz.q: What does /context show you about CLAUDE.md?

options.text: Whether the file loaded and how much context it costs.
options.why: The docs say to confirm a file loaded with /context under Memory files, and G6-06 uses it to see the cost.

options.text: A list of rules Claude broke in this session.
options.why: CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration; nothing tracks breaks.

options.text: The diff between CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.
options.why: There is no such diff; /context lists loaded memory files and their size.
